q: The treeable equivalence relations (those having a graphing that is a treeing, i.e., a.e. the graph is a tree) are important because:
opts: They include free group actions and are exactly the hyperfinite relations
Free groups produce treeings, and treeability is preserved under stable orbit equivalence — connecting free group actions to the cost invariant
exp: A relation is treeable if it has an a.e. acyclic graphing. Free actions of free groups Fₙ are treeable with cost n. Gaboriau showed cost is a stable OE invariant, and treeability is preserved under stable OE. This is key to distinguishing OE classes of free group actions.
